title: The Birth of Meycauayan
description: Franciscan friars Juan de Placencia and Diego Oropesa established Meycauayan as an early settlement during the Spanish colonial period. Its first church was built from nipa and bamboo and dedicated to St. Francis of Assisi.

title: A New Town Center Rises in Lagolo
description: The town center was transferred to Lagolo, where a concrete church was constructed. Meycauayan was then one of the largest towns in Bulacan and exercised political jurisdiction over several surrounding settlements.

title: Bocaue Becomes Part of Early Meycauayan
description: Bocaue became one of the towns under the political jurisdiction of the expansive early settlement of Meycauayan.

title: Meycauayan's Reach Extends to Polo
description: Polo, now known as Valenzuela, came under Meycauayan's political jurisdiction.

title: San Jose del Monte Joins Meycauayan's Historic Territory
description: San Jose del Monte became part of the territory governed under Meycauayan's political jurisdiction.

title: Obando Becomes Part of Meycauayan
description: Obando became one of the towns under Meycauayan's political jurisdiction.

title: Santa Maria de Pandi Joins Meycauayan's Territory
description: Santa Maria de Pandi was among the settlements placed under Meycauayan's political jurisdiction.

title: Meycauayan's Historic Territory Reaches Marilao
description: Marilao became one of the last towns listed under the political jurisdiction of historic Meycauayan.

title: Meycauayan Answers the Call for Freedom
description: Meycauayan joined the struggle for freedom through local revolutionaries including Gen. Andres Pacheco, Col. Ciriaco Contreras, Guillermo Bosque, and Liberato Exaltacion. Their efforts continued until the Philippines gained independence in 1898.

title: The Fire That Changed Poblacion
description: A major fire razed the entire town center in Poblacion, causing extensive property losses and setting back the municipality's development. Meycauayan took several years to recover from the destruction.

title: Meycauayan Rises Again
description: With assistance from the provincial and national governments, Meycauayan rebuilt and rehabilitated its infrastructure. These improvements renewed local development and strengthened the municipality's economic foundation.

title: A New Era as a First-Class Municipality
description: Meycauayan's stronger economic base enabled it to attain the status of a first-class municipality.

title: Meycauayan Becomes a City
description: On December 10, voters ratified Meycauayan's conversion into a component city under Republic Act No. 9356, making it Bulacan's third city. Meycauayan has since become a major economic and industrial hub in Bulacan and Region III.
